tree: Giant Tingle Tree (red tingle, Eucalyptus jacksonii)
place: Hilltop Road, Walpole-Nornalup National Park, WA
light: WEAK (brightness 97, colour 0.12, blown 6%): daylight and colour, bright sky behind the crown
why: Looking up a fire-hollowed red tingle, the trunk and crown both readable, in daylight and colour. Rough fibrous red-brown bark and a burnt hollow trunk fit red tingle. The geotag (-34.9831, 116.7897) is about 60 m from the Giant Tingle Tree on Hilltop Road (ExplorOz -34.9826, 116.7900), and the description gives over 22 m girth. This is the Giant Tingle Tree, NOT the Valley of the Giants, despite the filename. On a wide crop the centre band is the black hollow framed by the trunk walls, which is how this tree is known.

tree: Valley of the Giants red tingles (site, no named tree)
place: Valley of the Giants, Walpole-Nornalup National Park, WA
why: Looks steeply up a fire-scarred tingle trunk under a white sky, with only thin branches of crown. The file names the site but no tree (Forest Lord, Pleated Lady, Grey Bark and others are all unmatched), there is no geotag, and it is 540x720. It could do for a site-level entry, not for a named tree.

tree: Valley of the Giants red tingles (site, no named tree)
place: Walpole-Nornalup National Park, WA (no finer location)
why: A boardwalk through the base of a hollow tingle: base only, no crown, and neither the tree nor the site is named (the description only says Walpole-Nornalup NP). Fails the frame rule and the which-trunk rule.

tree: Valley of the Giants red tingles (site, no named tree)
why: A good straight trunk and crown against blue sky, but the file has no author, no description and no place (the last uploader is Rotatebot), so the attribution cannot be recorded and the trunk cannot be placed.

tree: Valley of the Giants red tingles (site, no named tree)
why: Only the hollow buttressed base over a boardwalk, with no crown in frame, and the tree and site are unnamed.

A massive grey, rough-barked trunk fills the frame, with the main limbs and canopy readable above, under blue sky; a person beside it gives the scale. The bark and form fit tuart. The file is named and described as the Wonnerup Giant by a big-tree hunter (Thyacine, who also took The Tyrant). Its only weakness is resolution: 448x598 covers the 330 bucket but not 500 or 960.

place: King River Road (Hillgrove), near Wyndham, WA
light: OK (brightness 116, colour 0.33); sun flare at the top edge only
why: An unmistakable boab: bottle trunk, spreading limbs, fruits hanging, two people for scale, blue sky. Carved names cover the trunk and the hollow opening sits at its base, matching the verify notes (engravings, lightning-broken top). It is described as the Boab Prison Tree, Wyndham, and there is only one there. At 4288x2848, the centre band holds the trunk and its doorway.

tree: The Ada Tree (mountain ash, Eucalyptus regnans)
place: Ada Tall Trees Reserve, near Powelltown, VIC
why: A generic stand of young-ish mountain ash with no single tree dominating. It is geotagged at Powelltown village (-37.8608, 145.7447), about 11 km from the Ada Tree pin (-37.8169, 145.8688), and the description only says 'Mountain Ash near Powelltown'. Not the Ada Tree, and no other Commons file of it was found.

tree: The Gloucester Tree (karri, Eucalyptus diversicolor), pem_001
why: Looking up a straight karri: the spiral of climbing pegs, the lookout cabin and the full crown against blue sky. The pale, smooth, patchy bark fits karri. The file is named as the Gloucester Tree and geotagged in Gloucester NP (-34.44761, 116.05668), about 260 m from our pin, and the base photo is tagged in the same place. That puts it in Gloucester NP, not on the Dave Evans or Diamond peg trees. The centre band shows the pegged trunk.
The right tree (named, pegs visible, crown readable), but it is 768x1024 under a grey sky, so the La Rosa file wins. Keep it as a backup if that one ever goes.
Only the base with its pegs and a warning sign, no crown. A good second photo for a photos[] gallery, but not a lead.
A forest view where the Gloucester Tree is one of several karri trunks and has to be searched for. Too distant to qualify.
A close-up of the trunk bark and pegs at a steep angle, with a hand intruding at the bottom right and no crown. It is the right tree (named), but it fails the frame rule.
The view down from the cabin, with a hand and the canopy below. The tree is not the subject.
Not downloaded. The description says it is a view through the hole in the cabin floor at the top, so the tree cannot be the subject. Rejected on that description; it can never be an approval.

The right tree (named 'The Tyrant, the largest known karri'). The enormous base fills the square frame and a man gives the scale, but the crown is entirely out of frame and the bark is in shade, so it fails 'crown and trunk both readable'. It is the only Commons file of the Tyrant.

tree: Mountain blue gum at Woodford (Eucalyptus deanei)
place: behind 20 Mile Hollow Cafe, Woodford, Blue Mountains, NSW
why: A black-and-white silhouette of an upper crown against cloud, with no trunk base. The description only says 'Eucalyptus tree behind 20 Mile Hollow Cafe', so it does not settle that this is the big blue gum.

tree: Mountain blue gum (Eucalyptus deanei), Blue Mountains
place: Blue Mountains National Park, NSW (site not given)
why: Looks up a tall, smooth, pale deanei trunk into its crown: right species, colour, daylight. But it is a 320x480 scan of a 1995 print, too small for any card, and its description (78 m, measured by Nicolle) names no site, so it cannot be tied to the Woodford tree.
